Whistleblower Series Draft v3

Prepared by Investigations Desk
Status: Draft for editorial review only

This draft reconstructs events surrounding facilities vendor Orion Facilities Group and subsequent whistleblower allegations.

Timeline narrative:
On January 12, 2025, internal auditor Maya Chen flagged unusual vendor invoices linked to Orion Facilities Group and escalated the issue to finance leadership.
On February 3, 2025, procurement manager Daniel Ruiz approved a second wave of emergency maintenance contracts without competitive bids.
On February 18, 2025, a facilities technician reported that several billed repair visits never occurred at the Harbor Point site.
On March 1, 2025, an anonymous whistleblower complaint was submitted through the ethics hotline alleging invoice inflation and retaliation.
On March 7, 2025, compliance opened a preliminary review and requested supporting documents from procurement and accounts payable.
On March 19, 2025, finance staff identified duplicate invoice numbers across three Orion submissions totaling $184,000.
On April 9, 2025, senior leadership was briefed on the allegations and authorized an external forensic audit.
On April 21, 2025, Orion's contract access was suspended pending the audit.
On May 2, 2025, former procurement staff member Leah Patel said she was reassigned after raising concerns about rushed approvals.

Additional reporting notes:
The internal review team interviewed the whistleblower on February 26, 2025, along with two finance analysts.
Another section states finance first discovered the duplicate numbering pattern during the March 7, 2025 document request phase.
A later paragraph says Orion continued receiving work orders until April 30, 2025.
Leah Patel is also described elsewhere as having been reassigned in mid-February 2025.

Editorial note: reconcile chronology before publication.
